paraphrase: At the Buddha's bidding Aṅgulimāla makes an act of truth for a woman in difficult labour: 'Since I was born with the noble birth I do not recall intentionally depriving a living being of life; by this truth may you and your child be well' — and she was well.

paraphrase: Struck by clods and stones on alms round, Aṅgulimāla is told: bear it, brahmin; you are experiencing here and now the result of deeds for which you might have been tormented in hell for many years.

paraphrase: The Buddha walks on while the bandit Aṅgulimāla, running with all his strength, cannot catch him; the Buddha explains: 'I have stopped, having laid aside violence towards all beings; you are unrestrained'; Aṅgulimāla throws away his weapons and goes forth.

paraphrase: 'Stop, ascetic!' 'I have stopped, Aṅgulimāla; you too stop.'
